newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks cap bullish week with flat close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks cap bullish week with flat close.

text.p: Argentine stocks gave back early gains to close virtually flat Friday as players locked in profits ahead of the year's final session, dealers said.
"We saw some volatility today as year-end selling caused the market to stall, which is logical after an eight-session rise," said Gabriel Armando of brokers Galicia Valores.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV still managed its fourth consecutive record high for 1996, closing up 0.02 percent at 650.23 and showing a weekly gain of 3.6 percent.
Brokers said the market might ease slightly Monday, the last trading day of this year on the bolsa.
"There are juicy profits to be snatched, but the bourse remains very solid and has conquered key resistance levels," said an analyst at a foreign-based brokerage.
He said equities were underpinned by the bond market, which rallied again Friday on the back of a moderate drop in the U.S. long bond yield.
Traders atributed the bond rally also partly to talk of a massive government bond issue in January.
"It's a combination of local and foreign factors, including the right economic data in both cases -- overall a good scenario despite any near-term correction," said Armando.
The broad market index closed unchanged Friday, with winners outpacing losers 42 to 15 and 17 stocks ending flat.
Floor volume picked up by three million pesos to 24.9 million, while over-the-counter deals eased to 72.6 million pesos from 75 million Thursday.

Top main-tier performances were in banks and the auto sector. Banco Francs and Banco de Galicia advanced 2.2 percent and 1.6 percent, respectively, while carmakers Ciadea and Sevel jumped 2.9 percent and 2.0 percent each, recouping losses blamed earlier this week on an import tariff row with Brazil.

MerVal losses were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, construction company Polledo and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which shed 3.6 percent, 1.9 percent and 1.6 percent, respectively.
